name: Two Normal Things and a Swerve
why_it_works: A list of three makes the brain predict the pattern. Two sensible items lock the prediction in, so a ridiculous third item breaks it and triggers a laugh of surprise. The deadpan justification afterwards makes the viewer replay it, and the brand item sits right next to the laugh.

hook.pattern: Promise a practical checklist of exactly three things for a moment the audience cares about.
examples: Nobody tells you the three things you need before {{occasion}}.
Before {{occasion}}, you need exactly three things. Number three matters most.

variables.name: occasion
variables.description: A relatable moment the audience prepares for

variables.name: normal_1
variables.description: First sensible item, ideally the brand's product or service

variables.name: swerve
variables.description: Third item: absurd, harmless, oddly specific
variables.example: a laminated list of your three best jokes

variables.name: swerve_reason
variables.description: Deadpan justification for the absurd item, ending back on the brand
variables.example: We can't fix the jokes. We can fix the fade.

variables.name: offer
variables.description: What the viewer gets for acting

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 flat-lay on a wooden counter at {{brand}}: three empty numbered cards 1, 2, 3, warm overhead light, clean negative space for text
Vertical close-up showing {{normal_1}} at {{brand}}, crisp detail, warm practical light, confident and polished, eye-level

beats.purpose: setup: item two, sensible, locks the pattern

visual.prompt: Vertical product-style photo of {{normal_2}} on the same counter, matching warm light and color grade, centered, clean background
Vertical clip, a hand slowly slides {{swerve}} into frame on the same counter with total seriousness, slow push-in, same warm light, played completely straight

beats.purpose: tag: deadpan justification back to the brand

visual.prompt: Vertical medium shot of a {{brand}} team member looking straight into the lens, arms crossed, zero smile, shop behind them softly lit

cta: {{offer}}. Tag the friend who needs item three.

craft.technique: Rule of three with a swerve (pattern break)
craft.notes: Setup: two sensible list items, read in the exact same cadence and framing, so the audience locks onto the pattern. Turn: item three is read in that same flat cadence but is absurd; the comedy is that nothing in the delivery changes. Tag: a deadpan justification that admits the brand can't help with item three but can with item one, which lands the brand on the laugh. Timing: give items one and two identical three-second beats so the rhythm becomes predictable; then pause one beat of silence after 'Three.' before revealing the swerve, and cut straight from the swerve to the unsmiling face with no music sting.

do_not: Make the swerve mean or about someone's looks, body or money
Signal the joke with a wink, laugh track or sound effect before the swerve lands
Change the camera framing on item three; the sameness is what sells it
Let the swerve be random with no link back; the tag must return to the brand
